hints: Look closely at the ester name, the second word tells you which carboxylic acid it came from.
Ethyl butanoate must split into a 2-carbon alcohol part and a 4-carbon acid part, while butyl ethanoate does the opposite.
Remember only acid hydrolysis gives the free carboxylic acid, alkaline hydrolysis gives the carboxylate salt instead.
walkthrough:
**Decode the ester name**

Think of an ester as alcohol part + acid part. The first word is the alkyl group from the alcohol, the second word is the alkanoate from the carboxylic acid.

$$\text{alkyl alkanoate} \rightarrow \text{alcohol (alkyl part) + carboxylic acid (alkanoate part)}$$

**Compare acid and alkaline hydrolysis**

Acid hydrolysis with dilute $\text{H}^+$ gives you the free carboxylic acid plus the alcohol. Alkaline hydrolysis with $\text{NaOH}$ gives you the carboxylate salt plus the alcohol, not the free acid.

$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOH + R'OH}$$
$$\text{RCOOR' + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{R'OH}$$

**Apply to this question**

We want $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, butanoic acid. That must come from a butanoate ester, so we need ethyl butanoate, and we need acid conditions to get the free acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

options.A: Acid hydrolysis does give a free acid plus alcohol, but butyl ethanoate splits to ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and butanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). The acid part is ethanoate, not butanoate.
options.B: Wrong on two counts. Butyl ethanoate contains the ethanoate fragment, not butanoate, and alkaline conditions give ethanoate salt ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$) plus butanol, not any free carboxylic acid.
options.C: Ethyl butanoate contains the butanoate fragment ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}$). Acid hydrolysis restores it as free butanoic acid plus ethanol. This is exactly what we want.
options.D: Ethyl butanoate has the right carbon skeleton, but alkaline hydrolysis with $\text{NaOH}$ gives sodium butanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$) plus ethanol. No free butanoic acid is formed, a classic trap.
